Direct-pair adjudication:
I support 21 proposals as necessary protection against the actual unrestricted labels. Ambiguity need occur in only one meaning direction for the symmetric guard to be warranted.

• キロ–キログラム and キロ–キロメートル: independently documented shortenings. キロ–千: the separate prefix sense means 1000 and permits “тысяча” as an answer to bare キロ. This does not make キロ a numeral/counter replacement or require exclusions among all measurement units. Computing 1024 is not adopted teaching.

• いくら–幾つ: their actual generic “сколько” labels overlap despite different Japanese constructions. いくら–何人 and 幾つ–何人 are separately justified by broad “сколько” versus “сколько человек”; neither teaches free Japanese headcount substitution.

• たくさん–多い, たくさん–大勢 and 大勢–多い: each has independent quantity overlap. Different syntax does not disambiguate these context-free Russian labels. 大勢 remains people-specific.

• たくさん–結構: directly supported by the enough/refusal sense, not merely their shared topic. Their lessons retain the different pragmatic qualifications.

• 大勢–人: “люди” is broad enough to be a reasonable label for the crowd denotation; 人 itself need not assert numerousness.

• 大勢–組 and 大勢–団体: the actual broad “группа” labels can describe a large group of people. 大勢で and the full support lessons supply direct grounds; Russian группа does not inherently require a small or institutional group. This is not a class/organization clique.

• もっと–より: direct adverbial “больше/более” overlap. Particle comparison and formal-source より remain distinct uses.

• 最初–出発: supported narrowly by the actual broad “начало” versus accepted “начало пути.” The complete 出発 lesson explicitly teaches the beginning of travel. Its dictionary object proves departure/leaving, not every generic beginning; that stronger claim is rejected. No arrival/ordering clique follows.
